module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures in Complexity Theory

This file contains formal statements of some of the main open conjectures
in complexity theory, including

- the P vs NP problem
- the NP vs coNP problem

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P_versus_NP_problem)
- [The Clay Institute](https://www.claymath.org/millennium/p-vs-np/)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ComplexityTheory

/--
**P ≠ NP**:

The conjecture that the complexity classes P and NP are not equal.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 68]
theorem P_ne_NP : P ≠ NP := by sorry

/--
**NP ≠ coNP**:

The conjecture that the complexity classes NP and coNP are not equal.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 68]
theorem NP_ne_coNP : NP ≠ coNP := by sorry

/--
The theorem that the set of complements of languages in P is itself P.

This can be proven by observing that the boolean negation function is computable in polynomial time,
and that compositions of poly-time computable functions are also poly-time computable.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 68]
theorem coP_eq_P :
    { L | Lᶜ ∈ P } = P := by
  sorry

/--
The theorem that P is a subset of NP.

This can be proven by observing that for any language in P,
we can construct a verifier that ignores the witness and simply runs the poly-time decider for the
language.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 68]
theorem P_subset_NP :
    P ⊆ NP := by
  sorry

/--
The theorem that P is a subset of coNP.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 68]
theorem P_subset_coNP :
    P ⊆ coNP := by
  rw [coNP, ← coP_eq_P]
  simp only [Set.ofPred_subset_ofPred]
  intros L hL
  exact P_subset_NP hL

end ComplexityTheory

reformulations.difference: The imported classes use Boolean characteristic functions on binary strings, canonical bitstring encodings, and Mathlib's finite-control stack-machine model rather than Cook's languages over arbitrary finite alphabets and single-tape machines.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Cook explicitly permits reduction to a binary alphabet and polynomially equivalent machine models. Boolean characteristic functions correspond bijectively to languages. The concrete encodings are efficiently invertible and have lengths 3|x| and 6|x|+3|w|+1, so they preserve polynomial bounds. Although FinTM2 permits infinite auxiliary alphabets, only finitely many symbols are reachable: auxiliary stacks start empty, and finitely many push instructions draw their symbols from functions of a finite internal state. Thus these machines admit ordinary finite-alphabet simulations with polynomial overhead. The NP definition has the standard uniform polynomial-time verifier and polynomially bounded existential witness. These choices preserve P, NP, and coNP, hence both separation conjectures.

reformulations.difference: The source describes P as closed under complementation; Lean states {L | Lᶜ ∈ P} = P.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Complementation of Boolean-valued decision problems is pointwise negation and is involutive. Closure gives both inclusions: apply closure to L for one direction and to Lᶜ for the other. Conversely, the displayed equality immediately gives closure. This equivalence, and equality of the comprehension with the image of P under complementation, were proved in the scratch checks.

sources_consulted: Stephen Cook, The P Versus NP Problem, especially §1, the coNP discussion in §2, §3, and the appendix: https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/pvsnp.pdf
review.notes: Checked all five declarations and their imported definitions. The sources still record both separation conjectures as open and support all three textbook relations. Both scratch files compile without errors or warnings. Independent, sorry-free checks establish the encoding lengths, complement semantics, the zero witness-bound case, impossibility of a zero-step halting computation, and membership of the empty and universal languages in P, NP, and coNP. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/boundaries.lean. No repository files were edited.
